newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BEVAN AND WAUGH CLINCH SERIES WIN FOR AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEVAN AND WAUGH CLINCH SERIES WIN FOR AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Michael Bevan and Steve Waugh hammered South Africa into submission at Centurion Park on Thursday as Australia clinched the seven-match one day international series with a game to spare.
Replying to South Africa's daunting total of 284 for seven, Australia reached 287 for five, wrapping up victory by five wickets with six balls remaining.
Australia have a 4-2 series lead after winning the last three matches in a row and Sunday's final encounter in Bloemfontein is now an irrelevance.

Bevan made a magnificent 103 from just 94 balls with eight fours and a six, his maiden one day international century, and was the dominant partner in a record Australian fourth wicket stand of 189. Waugh made up for a second ball duck by twin brother Mark by smacking 89 from 102 balls with six fours and a six.

Bevan put himself in line for the man of the series award as he and Waugh rebuilt the innings from 58 for three in the 14th over. He reached his third half-century of the series in 54 balls and then launched an assault on the South African bowlers by racing to his century in another 39.
Waugh had the distinction of breaking one of his own records when he cut Rudi Bryson for six over point to take the stand past the 173 he and Dean Jones made against Pakistan in Perth in 1986/87.

Paceman Bryson ended the stand soon afterwards when he trapped Bevan lbw, and Waugh went the same way to Shaun Pollock four overs later. But with the score at 262 for five in the 46th over the pair had broken the back of Australia's task and with it South Africa's spirit.
The home side seemed to have done enough to level the series when they put together the second highest total scored by South Africa at one day level.

Daryll Cullinan (89) and Hansie Cronje (80) were also in record breaking mood as they put on 153 for the third wicket, beating the previous best for the country by Cullinan and Gary Kirsten against the UAE in last year's World Cup.

Cullinan made his runs from 96 balls with eight boundaries and Cronje from 81 with six fours and two sixes. But the pair were dismissed in successive overs and a total that looked set to be beyond 300 fell crucially short.

It needed a bright cameo of 33 in 23 balls from Pollock to get his side back on track. Pollock also starred with the ball having Mark Waugh caught at point from the second ball of the Australian reply and then getting Greg Blewett caught at deep quare leg for 21.
Cronje chipped in by bowling Stuart Law for 31, but from that point on South Africa's hopes slid downhill as Bevan and Waugh re-emphasised the gap in class between the two sides.
